strategy.action_description: Keep d660c1aa stage1 exactly as the current best tiled-dequant implementation, and replace only stage2_output_kernel with a route-parallel grouped down-projection tile. Treat each valid local route as an M row, use CTAs over route tiles x hidden-column tiles with a cooperative split over I, reuse the d660c1aa scale-tiled FP4 decode for gemm2 weights, multiply by topk_weights, atomicAdd into a FP32 out_accum buffer, and finalize to bf16. Avoid changing gate/up stage1 in this child so the effect is attributable to the down-projection grouped GEMM boundary.
strategy.evidence_chain: In d660c1aa, stage2 still launches only T*H output threads and each thread serially loops over TOPK and I, giving only 256 output threads for the smoke shape before serial work. The generation-1 full grouped-GEMM child reached 247.424 us but changed both stages, added scalar decode, and paid route compaction overhead. New finding: the FlashInfer reference material has a separate blockscaled contiguous grouped GEMM finalize-fusion kernel using tile_idx_to_expert_idx/token_id_mapping, which supports testing the down/finalize boundary independently instead of rewriting the whole MoE mainloop at once.
strategy.expected_impact: Medium. This should increase stage2 parallelism by using M=T*TOPK route rows instead of serial TOPK work per token/output column, while preserving the fastest known stage1. It is also a focused stepping stone toward full FlashInfer-style grouped GEMM finalize fusion.
strategy.risks: The FP32 out_accum memset, atomicAdd traffic, and finalize launch can erase the benefit for T=2. Atomic accumulation order may change bf16 rounding, although the prior grouped-GEMM child passed exact smoke correctness. Roll back by restoring d660c1aa stage2_output_kernel.

executor_result.action_description: Kept the d660c1aa stage1 gate/up path unchanged and replaced only the down-projection/output stage with a route-parallel grouped GEMM-style kernel over T*TOPK route rows, hidden-column tiles, and split-I scale tiles. The grouped kernel reuses the existing FP4 scale-tiled decode, applies topk_weights, atomically accumulates into an FP32 out_accum buffer, and a finalize kernel converts to bf16 output.
